findings.title: View permission on all groups grants group management
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates the all-groups resource with both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes. This method guards creation of top-level groups (`GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`) and is also used as the global management shortcut, so an administrator granted only the read-only `view` scope on the Groups resource can create groups and receive management access that should require `manage`. Evaluate only `MANAGE` here.

findings.title: Group member visibility lookup uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: `groupResource.getId()` is the ID of the authorization `Resource`, whereas group-scoped resources are stored with the Keycloak group ID as their name. Passing the resource ID to `hasPermission` causes `findByName(server, groupId)` to miss the scoped resource and fall back to the all-groups resource; adding that same authorization resource ID to `granted` also supplies IDs that do not match user group memberships. Consequently a caller with `view-members` or `manage-members` on a particular group will not get that group in the user-search group filter and cannot discover its members through user search (and may instead receive incorrect results when an all-groups policy exists). Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission evaluation and the returned group ID.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never upgraded with the new Groups scopes/resources
findings.body: `init` immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. After upgrading a realm that had FGAP v2 enabled before this change, that client therefore lacks the newly introduced `Groups` resource type and the `manage-membership`, `manage-members`, and `view-members` scopes. Creating a group-scoped permission then cannot resolve its scopes/resources (for example `getOrCreateResource` throws when a scope is absent), leaving the new feature unusable for existing realms. Add an upgrade/reconciliation path that creates missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client.
